5a098284ec1e: Your party: the main force of the centre-right camp, heir to Konstantinos Karamanlis: a member of the European People's Party, the backbone of business, pensioners, rural Greece, the Peloponnese and the islands. In the June 2023 election it won 40.6% and 158 seats thanks to the winner's bonus. Inside there is a “liberal” reformist wing and a “popular” right wing that Greek Solution and Samaras, expelled from the party in 2024, are pulling towards themselves. Weak spots: Tempi, OPEKEPE, the wiretapping, the cost of living and fatigue after seven years in power.
e452e1984e2e: Your party: a centrist technocratic movement created in 2022 by former economy and finance ministers Spajić and Milatović. The Europe Now programme doubled the minimum wage (to 450, then 600–800 €), abolished health contributions and raised pensions. At the 2023 election it came first (25.5%, 24 seats), but after President Milatović's departure and the expulsion of Justice Minister Milović the group has 19 MPs. Its base is young people, private-sector workers, Podgorica and Nikšić.
b6e7f5ade099: Your party: the country's main right-wing force: national conservatism, Macedonian identity and a "dignified" foreign policy with no concessions to Sofia. In the "Your Macedonia" bloc you won 58 seats and the 2025 local elections, taking 55 mayors out of 80. Your base is Macedonians in small towns and villages, pensioners, the security forces and the diaspora. Weak points are corruption scandals, the Kočani fire, slow construction and food inflation, while Levica breathes down your neck on the right.
f5eeaf6f7449: Your party: the liberal-progressive Democrats 66: city dwellers, young people, educated voters. You lead a minority cabinet: you have 66 seats of 150 and no majority in the Senate.
709cebc9e4d9: Your party: the historic Bratianu liberals, today a centre-right EPP party. In the 2024 elections it won only 13.2% and 49 seats, but after the 2025 elections its chair Ilie Bolojan, former mayor of Oradea and president of the Senate, became prime minister and the “face” of tough budget consolidation. Its base is the cities of Transylvania and the Banat, entrepreneurs and the middle class; in December 2025 PNL member Ciprian Ciucu won the Bucharest mayoral election. Its weak points are unpopular tax rises, frozen pensions and the eternal war of the local barons.
edc6e9262cd7: Your party: Smer, the largest force in Slovak politics of the last twenty years: “left” on the economy and conservative on values, sovereigntist in relations with the EU and Ukraine. Its base is pensioners, workers in small towns and villages, especially in the Trenčín, Banská Bystrica and Prešov regions. In the 2023 elections it won 22.9% and 42 seats; its programme is the 13th pension, energy aid, “peace instead of weapons” and a fight against the “liberal” press and NGOs.
4381997bb746: Your party: a centre-left and national movement that grew out of street protests against “colonial” UN administration and the corruption of the old parties of former KLA commanders. In power since 2021; in the election of 28 December 2025 it won 51.1% and 57 seats, the best result in the country’s history. The list includes President Vjosa Osmani’s “Guxo” and Mimoza Kusari-Lila’s “Alternativa”. Its base is young people, the diaspora in Germany and Switzerland, public sector workers and poor suburbs. Its principles are “sovereignty over the whole territory”, the fight against corruption and a hard line in relations with Belgrade, which irritates Brussels and Washington.
